subject: ENG
question:
Choose the **correct indirect speech** conversion of the sentence.

"Scientists say, 'Habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort'".

options.text: Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort.
Scientists said that habits emerged because the brain was constantly looking for ways to save effort.
Scientists say habits had emerged because the brain constantly looked for ways to save effort.
Scientists have said that habits emerge as the brain constantly looks for ways to save effort.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb in Present Tense:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"say"** is in the present tense. According to grammar rules, if the reporting verb is in the present, future, or present perfect tense, the tense of the verbs in the reported speech does not change.
 
 
 
• **Universal Truth/Scientific Fact:**
 
 
• The statement *"Habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort"* is a **scientific fact**. Scientific facts and general truths typically remain in the present tense when reported, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is used to introduce the reported clause in an assertive sentence.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks and the comma following the reporting verb are removed.
 
• The sentence ends with a simple full stop.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Scientists said that habits emerged because the brain was constantly looking for ways to save effort." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it unnecessarily changes the reporting verb to the past tense ("said") and shifts the scientific fact into the past tense ("emerged," "was looking").
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Scientists say habits had emerged because the brain constantly looked for ways to save effort." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it uses the past perfect ("had emerged") and simple past ("looked"), which alters the original meaning and violates the rule for present-tense reporting verbs.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Scientists have said that habits emerge as the brain constantly looks for ways to save effort." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the reporting verb to the present perfect ("have said") and modifies the original sentence structure (replacing "because" with "as").

question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.**

Burkin once had a client who had a breast tumour that was not spotted until it had __________ and she wanted to sue her internist for the delayed __________ and was also aware it was her _______ who was potentially at fault.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **M​etastasized, diagnosis, radiologist.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The context of the sentence suggests that the client had a breast tumour that was not detected in time and had spread to other parts of the body.
 
• The words that would fit best in the blanks are "**metastasized**" and "**diagnosis**."
 
• **Metastasized **refers to the spread of cancer cells from the original site of the cancer to other parts of the body. This process is called metastasis.
 
• **Diagnosis **refers to the identification or determination of the nature and cause of a particular health condition or disease based on a patient's symptoms, medical history, and physical examination, as well as diagnostic tests or procedures. 
 
• The third word would be a medical professional who may have been responsible for the delayed diagnosis.
 
• "**Radiologist**" is the most appropriate option in this context because radiologists specialize in using medical imaging techniques such as X-rays and mammograms to diagnose and treat diseases.
 
• **Example sentences:**
 
 
• **Metastasis **is the spread of cancer cells from one part of the body to another.
 
• A delayed **diagnosis **can have serious consequences for a patient's health.
 
• The **radiologist **examined the X-ray to determine the cause of the patient's symptoms.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence:__ ***Burkin once had a client who had a breast tumour that was not spotted until it had __**metastasized**__* *and she wanted to sue her internist for the delayed __**diagnosis**__* *and was also aware it was her __**radiologist**__* *who was potentially at fault.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• **Other options:**
 
• **Metamorphosed **means to undergo a transformation in form or nature.
 
 
• For example, a caterpillar **metamorphoses **into a butterfly.
 
 
 
• **Necropsy **is an autopsy performed on an animal to determine the cause of death.
 
 
• For example, a veterinarian may perform a **necropsy **on a deceased pet to determine the cause of illness.
 
 
 
• **Biopsy **is a medical procedure in which a sample of tissue is removed from the body for examination.
 
 
• For example, a **biopsy **may be performed on a suspicious mole to check for cancer cells.
 
 
 
• **Nephrologist** is a medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of kidney-related diseases.
 
• **Cardiologist**: This is a medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of heart-related diseases.
 
• The word "**metaphorised**" is not a common English word, and it is not found in most dictionaries. However, it could be interpreted as the past tense of "metaphorize," which means to use a metaphor or create a metaphorical comparison.
 
• **Autopsy**, also known as a post-mortem examination or necropsy, is a medical examination of a deceased person's body to determine the cause of death and to identify any underlying medical conditions that may have contributed to their death. 
 
• A **dermatologist **is a medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating conditions and diseases related to the skin, hair, and nails. 
 
• **Metabolism **refers to the chemical processes that occur within a living organism to maintain life. When we say that a substance has been **metabolized**, it means that it has undergone chemical changes within the body as part of the metabolic process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the introductory phrase "Despite being accused," which is **part (P).**
 
• In English grammar, the verb "accused" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "of." This creates a logical mandatory pair between **part (P)** and **part (S)** ("of misconduct").
 
• Following the introductory dependent clause (PS), the main clause must start with a subject. **Part (Q)** "they" serves as the subject of the sentence.
 
• **Part (R)** "remained silent" provides the predicate (action) for the subject, completing the thought logically and grammatically.

Therefore, the correct sequence is **PSQR**, forming the sentence: *"Despite being accused of misconduct, they remained silent."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2 (QRPS):** Although "They remained silent despite being accused of misconduct" is a grammatically valid sentence, in standardized tests, the structure beginning with the introductory phrase (PSQR) is typically favored to test clause recognition.
 
• **Option 4 (QSPR):** This arrangement is nonsensical as it places "of misconduct" immediately after the subject "they" without a connecting verb or context.

question:
**Arrange the passage correctly:**

(1) Push the door open.

(2) The door unlocks with a click.

(3) Turn the key clockwise.

(4) Insert the key in the lock.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **4 - 3 - 2 - 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sequence follows the **chronological logic** of opening a locked door. The process must begin by **inserting the key (4)** into the lock.
 
• After the key is inserted, the physical action required to engage the mechanism is to **turn the key (3)**.
 
• The immediate result of turning the key is that the locking bolt retracts, which is when **the door unlocks with a click (2)**.
 
• Only after the lock is fully disengaged can you perform the final step and **push the door open (1)**.

Therefore, the correct logical order is **4 - 3 - 2 - 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (3-4-2-1):** This is physically impossible because you cannot turn a key before it has been inserted into the lock.
 
• **Option 3 (4-2-3-1):** This suggests the door clicks and unlocks before the turning action happens, which reverses cause and effect.
 
• **Option 4 (2-3-4-1):** This implies the door is already unlocked before you even touch the key, making the insertion and turning steps redundant.

• **Option 3:** "Realistic" - This would imply the statement is accurate and straightforward, which the author questions.

• An antonym is a word that has the opposite meaning of another word.
 
• Therefore, the opposite of having the ability to make one's own decisions (autonomy) would be reliance on others to make decisions for you, which is captured by the word **'Dependence'.**
 
• **'Dependence' **signifies a state where someone relies on or needs something else; it contrasts with autonomy's emphasis on independence and self-direction.
 
• Considering virtual learning's advantage allows for self-paced learning, highlighting autonomy, the contrast would be a learning format where students are dependent on a structured schedule and possibly direct oversight.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Dependence."**

• It does not directly relate to autonomy or its opposite, making it an unsuitable option.
 
 
 
• Liberty is similar in meaning to autonomy, as it also deals with freedom and independence, making it a synonym rather than an antonym.
 
• Availability refers to being able to be used or obtained, which is irrelevant to the concept of autonomy or its direct opposite.

• Therefore, the opposite of keeping or maintaining something (retention) would be the act of giving up or releasing something, which is encapsulated by the word 'Relinquishment'.
 
• 'Relinquishment' signifies the act of voluntarily giving up, releasing, or abandoning something, making it the direct opposite of retention, which implies holding on to or keeping.
 
• The passage discusses how online courses are associated with higher retention rates, implying students continue their courses until completion.
 
• The opposite scenario would involve students abandoning or discontinuing their courses, therefore, making 'Relinquishment' the correct antonym.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** "Option 4".**

• It does not directly relate to the concept of retaining or its opposite.
 
 
 
• Preventive is an adjective that describes something designed to stop something bad from happening.
 
 
• While it talks about prevention, it doesn't directly contrast with the idea of retention or keeping.
 
 
 
• Retaining is actually a synonym of retention, as it also means to keep or hold on to something.

question: Which of the following statements concerning the effects of scientific advancements may be derived from the passage?

options.text: The development of renewable energy technologies has led to a complete elimination of greenhouse gas emissions.
Scientific innovations have the potential to revolutionise various sectors and improve efficiency in society.
There is no longer any need for human intelligence since AI has taken over every field.
The only way to solve problems with food security and renewable energy is through genetic engineering.

solution:
The correct answer is: **Scientific innovations have the potential to revolutionize various sectors and improve efficiency in society.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

This underscores the idea that scientific innovations can revolutionize various industries and enhance societal efficiency, directly aligning with option 2.
 
• **Why the other options are incorrect:**
 
 
• **Option 1 (The development of renewable energy technologies has led to a complete elimination of greenhouse gas emissions):** While the passage mentions that renewable energy technologies help to lower greenhouse gas emissions, it does not claim that they have completely eliminated these emissions.
 
• **Option 3 (There is no longer any need for human intelligence since AI has taken over every field):** The passage states that AI has caused a revolution in various sectors by accomplishing tasks previously requiring human intelligence, but it does not suggest that AI has entirely replaced the need for human intelligence.
 
• **Option 4 (The only way to solve problems with food security and renewable energy is through genetic engineering):** The passage discusses genetic engineering as one solution for issues related to food security and renewable energy but does not assert it as the sole solution. It also mentions other technologies, such as renewable energy sources and IoT, in addressing different problems.
 
 
 
• In **summary**, **option 2** accurately reflects the passage’s emphasis on the broad and profound impact of scientific innovations in revolutionizing various sectors and improving societal efficiency. **Options 1, 3, and 4** either misrepresent specific claims or overlook the comprehensive scope of advancements discussed in the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

subject: ENG
question:
Which of the following best describes the grammatical structure of the sentence:

"This deep connection between space and time implies that the passage of time is not universal but relative:"?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Complex sentence**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **complex sentence** consists of one independent clause and at least one dependent (subordinate) clause.
 
• In the given sentence, the **independent clause** is "This deep connection between space and time implies [something]." It can stand alone as a complete thought.
 
• The **dependent clause** is "that the passage of time is not universal but relative." This is a **noun clause** acting as the object of the verb "implies." It cannot stand alone as a complete sentence.
 
• The word **"that"** serves as the subordinating conjunction that links the dependent clause to the main independent clause.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Sentence:** Contains only one independent clause with a subject and a predicate (e.g., "Space and time are connected."). 
 
• **Compound Sentence:** Consists of two or more independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS) or a semicolon (e.g., "Space is vast, and time is relative.").
 
• **Compound-Complex Sentence:** Contains at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause (e.g., "Scientists studied the data, and they concluded that time is relative.").

question: In the sentence **"Gravity is no longer thought of as a force in the Newtonian sense but rather as the curvature of space-time..."**, what does the word **"curvature"** most likely refer to?

options.text: Bending of the path of planets only
Warping of the structure of space and time
Deformation of gravitational fields by energy

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) Defining "Curvature" in General Relativity.***

 
 
• In the context of Einstein's theory, "curvature" refers to the geometric distortion of the four-dimensional continuum. The passage explicitly links this to the "**warping of space and time itself**," replacing the Newtonian idea of gravity as a traditional force.
 
 
 
• ***B) The role of mass and energy.***
 
 
• The text states that this curvature is "caused by the presence of mass and energy." This indicates that the very fabric of the universe is what is being altered, rather than individual physical objects folding or bending independently.
 
 
 
• ***C) Influence on motion and time.***
 
 
• The passage explains that objects follow "geodesics," which are paths dictated by this warping. This confirms that curvature is a structural property of the space-time fabric that governs how everything within it moves and experiences time.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Warping of the structure of space and time.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the curvature affects the space-time fabric in which objects exist, not the "folding" of the physical objects (like rocks or ships) themselves.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the term "only" makes this statement too restrictive; curvature affects all matter, energy, and even light, not just planets.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because while energy does cause the deformation, the passage defines gravity as the curvature of space-time itself, making Option 3 the most direct and accurate reflection of the text's definition.

• **Option 4, "pervasive,"** is a synonym of "prevalent" and therefore not an antonym. "Pervasive" means spreading widely throughout an area or group, and can be used in similar contexts as **"prevalent."**

• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

Nostalgic - This tone would imply a longing or affection for the past. This passage does not indicate any such feelings, as it is centered around presenting facts about flamingos.

Reflective - A reflective tone would involve a level of personal insight, introspection, or contemplation, which is not present in this informative piece.

Satirical - A satirical tone would involve the use of humor, irony, or exaggeration to expose or criticize. This passage is straightforward and does not employ these techniques.

**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word kindness from the given sentence:**

Laboni is a perfect combination of intelligence, kindness, honesty, and patience and feels no animosity towards others.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Animosity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct **antonym **of **"kindness"** in the given sentence is** 4) animosity.**
 
• **Kindness **refers to **the quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate towards others.** It is an inherently positive trait that involves treating others with respect and empathy. The opposite of kindness would be a negative trait that involves treating others poorly or with hostility.
 
 
• Example: She showed **kindness **by helping the elderly woman carry her groceries to her car.
 
 
 
• **"Animosity"** is the correct **antonym **in this context because it refers to **a feeling of strong dislike or hostility towards someone. **This is the opposite of kindness, which involves treating others with respect and empathy. Therefore, if Laboni feels no animosity towards others, it implies that she is kind and friendly towards them.
 
 
• Example: There was a strong **animosity **between the two political parties, which made it difficult for them to work together.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are not appropriate antonyms in this context:
 
• **"Patience"** is not an appropriate antonym of kindness because it does not have an inherently negative connotation. While patience involves waiting calmly and enduring discomfort or inconvenience without complaint, it does not involve hostility or ill-treatment towards others.
 
• **"Honesty"** is not an appropriate antonym of kindness because it does not have an inherently negative connotation either. While honesty involves telling the truth and being straightforward, it does not involve treating others poorly or with hostility.
 
• **"Intelligence" **is not an appropriate antonym of kindness because it is not related to how one treats others. Intelligence refers to the ability to learn, understand, and apply knowledge and information, and it does not involve treating others positively or negatively.

__

• **"Only good decisions can be agreed on"** is a statement of preference or principle, not a phrase used to express skepticism.
 
• **"I do not like to buy"** expresses a personal dislike towards the act of purchasing, which is unrelated to the idiom's metaphorical meaning of not being convinced.

**Direction: In the following sentence, an idiom is highlighted. Select the alternative which best describes its use in the sentence.**

He got a job in the Railways __through the back door__

options.text: Entered the office through the back entrance
The main door is under repair
In an indirect or unfair way

solution:
Here the correct answer is** In an indirect or unfair way.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom** "through the back door" **is **option 4: "In an indirect or unfair way."**
 
• The idiom **"through the back door" **is commonly **used to describe a situation where someone gets something, such as a job, promotion, or opportunity, in an indirect or unfair way, often by using personal connections or influence.** The person may not have met the usual qualifications or gone through the standard selection process.
 
• For example, if someone says **"He got the job through the back door,"** it means that he did not get the job on merit, but rather through some kind of personal influence or unfair advantage.
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is saying that the person got a job in the Railways through the back door, which implies that the person did not go through the usual selection process, but instead used some kind of personal influence or connections to secure the job.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**, "Entered the office through the back entrance," is a literal interpretation of the idiom and does not convey the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 2**, "Without appearing to others," is not related to the idiom and is not a commonly used expression.
 
• **Option 3,** "The main door is under repair," is a possible interpretation of the literal meaning of the words "through the back door," but it does not fit the context of the sentence, which is about securing a job in an indirect or unfair way.

In two minds

Here the correct answer is** Holding conflicting opinions.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence is **option 4: "holding conflicting opinions."**
 
• The idiom **"of two minds"** means** to be undecided or uncertain about something because one is torn between two conflicting opinions or options.**
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is uncertain whether to go to the convention or not, indicating that he/she has conflicting thoughts or opinions about it.
 
• **Example sentences:**
 
 
• I'm **of two minds** about whether to accept the job offer or not.
 
• She was **of two minds** about buying the expensive dress, but in the end, she decided to go for it.
 
• He's **of two minds **about whether to invest in the stock market or keep his money in a savings account.
 
 
 
• **Option 1**, **"holding a negative opinion,"** is incorrect because "of two minds" does not indicate a negative opinion, but rather a state of being undecided or uncertain.
 
• **Option 2**, **"holding a clear opinion,"** is incorrect because "of two minds" implies the opposite of having a clear opinion or stance on something.
 
• **Option 3**, **"holding a positive opinion," **is incorrect for the same reason as option 2. The idiom "of two minds" does not imply a positive or negative opinion, but rather a state of uncertainty or indecision.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.**

All eyes turned to him because he was the only person who could __stave off__ the impending war.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Prevent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom **"stave off" **in the given sentence is **"prevent."**
 
• **Stave off: **to prevent or delay something unpleasant or dangerous from happening.
 
 
• Example: Taking vitamin C supplements can help** stave off **colds and flu.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase** "stave off"** is used to describe the action that the person in question could take to prevent the impending war. Therefore, the correct answer is **"prevent."**
 
• **"Prevent" **means to stop something from happening or to avoid something undesirable from occurring.
 
 
• Example: Wearing a helmet while riding a bike can **prevent **head injuries in case of an accident.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "invoke,"** does not fit the context of the sentence because there is no indication that the person in question is calling upon a higher power or authority for help.
 
• **Option 3, "draw,"** does not fit the context of the sentence because there is no indication that the person in question is attracting or bringing anything closer.
 
• **Option 4, "provoke," **does not fit the context of the sentence because there is no indication that the person in question is inciting a reaction or causing anger.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Invoke: **to call upon a higher power, authority, or spirit for help or inspiration.

 
 
• Example: The priest **invoked **the name of God in his prayer.
 
 
 
• **Draw**: to attract or bring something or someone closer; to cause a particular reaction or response.
 
 
• Example: The new shopping mall **drew **large crowds of shoppers on its opening day.
 
 
 
• **Provoke:** to incite or stimulate a strong reaction or response; to cause anger or annoyance.
 
 
• Example: The athlete's arrogant behavior **provoked **his opponents.

• It is often associated with the American Dream, the idea that anyone can achieve success and prosperity through hard work and determination, regardless of social status or background.
 
• The phrase is believed to have been first coined by Horatio Alger Jr., an American writer of children's books in the 19th century, who wrote many stories about young people from humble backgrounds who became successful through hard work and perseverance.

question:
The policeman said, "Don't worry. We'll find your stolen car. We'll leave no stone unturned."

What does the phrase "We'll leave no stone unturned" mean in the policeman's statement?

options.text: They will return the car immediately.
They will not investigate the case.
They will only search in a few places.

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**, i.e., "They will search everywhere thoroughly."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"leave no stone unturned"** means to make every possible effort to achieve something or to search for something thoroughly. • **Example:** The rescue team left no stone unturned in their search for the missing hikers.
 

 
• **"Thoroughly"** refers to doing something in an exhaustive and detailed way, without missing any part. • **Example:** The teacher thoroughly checked all the students' assignments for errors.
 

 
• Hence, in the given context, the police assure that they will make every effort to find the stolen car, which aligns with the meaning of "leave no stone unturned."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: They will return the car immediately.**: This option is incorrect because the phrase "leave no stone unturned" refers to making an exhaustive effort, not an immediate action.
 
 
• **Example:** If they knew where the car was, they would have returned it immediately, but they still need to search thoroughly.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: They will not investigate the case.**: This option is incorrect as the phrase means the exact opposite — it emphasizes thorough investigation rather than avoiding it.
 
 
• **Example:** The officers cannot leave the case uninvestigated; they must leave no stone unturned.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: They will only search in a few places.**: This is incorrect because "leave no stone unturned" implies searching everywhere, not just in limited places.
 
 
• **Example:** A limited search would not fulfill their promise of leaving no stone unturned.

Social organisation where males are heads of families

are think that the writer has
have thinking that the writer is
will think that the writer is

solution:

__
 
• The correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is **"will think that the writer is."**
 
• The original sentence is in the present continuous tense ("reading"), so we need a future tense to indicate a future event.
 
• **"Will think" **is the correct **future tense** to use here, as it indicates that the action (thinking) will occur in the future.
 
• The other options either use the wrong tense or incorrect verb forms.
 
• **Option 1** uses** "will have think,"** which is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 2** uses** "are think,**" which is also incorrect.
 
• **Option 3** uses **"have thinking," **which is the present perfect tense and is not appropriate for this sentence.
 
• Therefore, **option 4** is the most appropriate and grammatically correct option.

**Correct Sentence:**__* Anyone reading these lines __**will think that the writer is**__ very sad.*

Reading shall make a man wise

The correct answer is "**Reading makes a man wise**"

__
 
• The most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is: "**Reading has the capacity to make a man wise**."
 
• This option correctly conveys the intended meaning of the original sentence that **reading has the potential or ability to make a person wise**.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect as it does not use the correct **subject-verb agreement** (**make should be changed to makes to agree with the singular subject "Reading"**).
 
• **Option 3 and 4 **are also incorrect as they suggest an **obligation **or a **certainty **that reading will make a man wise, which is not necessarily true.
 
• The original sentence is suggesting that reading has the potential to make a person wise, but that potential is limited if one only reads textbooks, like living in a room of the same height, implying that one needs to read more broadly to truly gain wisdom.
 
• Thus, ***option 1*** is the correct answer.

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word.**

The report claimed that a __consensus__ was growing against the absolute authority in the country.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Generally accepted agreement'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Consensus** refers to** a general agreement among a group of people or a community about a certain issue or decision. **In this context, the report claims that there is a growing agreement among people against absolute authority in the country.
 
• Hence,** option 1,** which means a generally accepted agreement, is the correct meaning of the word 'consensus' in this context.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 2, **which means a difference of opinion, is the opposite meaning of consensus.
 
• **Option 3**, which means the center of attraction, and **option 4**, which means systematically collected laws, are unrelated to the meaning of the word '**consensus**'. 

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** *Generally accepted agreement.*

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.**

Sugar ________ in water because it is made up of molecules of sucrose, a compound held together by relatively weak bonds. When the sucrose molecules mix with water, the water molecules ________ and break the bonds holding together the sugar molecule.
solution:
The correct answer is **1) melts; surround.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When sugar is added to water, it dissolves and forms a homogeneous solution.
 
• The process of dissolving involves breaking down the sugar crystals into individual molecules and allowing them to interact with the water molecules.
 
• The bonds that hold the sugar molecules together are relatively weak, and the water molecules can easily surround and separate them.
 
• The word** "melts"** accurately describes** the process of sugar dissolving in water.**
 
• **Melting **refers to **the process of a solid turning into a liquid due to the addition of heat.** In the case of sugar dissolving in water, heat is not required, but the process is similar in that the sugar crystals turn into a liquid-like state due to the interaction with the water molecules.
 
• The word **"surround" **accurately describes how the water molecules interact with the sugar molecules to dissolve them. The water molecules form hydrogen bonds with the sugar molecules, which allows them to surround and separate the individual molecules.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *Sugar __**melts**__* *in water because it is made up of molecules of sucrose, a compound held together by relatively weak bonds. When the sucrose molecules mix with water, the water molecules __**surround**__* *and break the bonds holding together the sugar molecule.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are not appropriate for this context:
 
• **"vanish; limit"** - Sugar does not vanish when it dissolves in water. It simply separates into individual molecules and becomes part of the water solution. The word **"limit" **does not make sense in this context.
 
• **"soften; grid" **- Sugar does not become softer when it dissolves in water, nor does it interact with a "**grid**" in any way. These words do not make sense in this context.
 
• **"disappear; edge"** - While sugar does disappear from view when it dissolves in water, the word "**disappear**" does not accurately describe the chemical process of dissolving. The word **"edge"** does not make sense in this context.

question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words.**

A disease that is found in a particular place and is difficult to get rid of.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Endemic'.

***__Key Points__**

 
• Let us explore the given options:-

 
 
• 'Chronic' is **(of an illness) persisting for a long time or constantly recurring**.

 
 
• Example: *If left untreated the condition may become **chronic***.
 
 
 
• 'Pandemic' is **(of a disease) prevalent over a whole country or the world**.
 
 
• Example: *All countries should immediately activate their **pandemic** preparedness plans*.
 
 
 
• 'Infection' is **the process of infecting or the state of being infected**.
 
 
• Example: *She has got an ear **infection***.
 
 
 
• 'Endemic' is **(of a disease or condition) regularly found among particular people or in a certain area**.
 
 
• Example: *Chest disease is **endemic** among miners in this area*.

 
 
 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.*

subject: ENG
question:
Choose the correct one-word substitution for:
"The study of the origin and history of words."
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Etymology .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Etymology** refers to the study of the origin of words and how their meanings and structures have evolved over time.
 
• It specifically examines the history of words, tracing their roots back to their earliest forms and languages.
 
• In contrast:
 
 
• **Philology** is the study of language in historical texts and its development over time.
 
• **Lexicography** deals with the compilation and writing of dictionaries.
 
• **Semantics** focuses on the meanings of words and their interpretation in context.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The study of the origin and history of words is called **Etymology**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Philology:**
 
 
• Derived from Greek, meaning "love of words."
 
• Broader than etymology, as it covers the study of language, literature, and historical texts.
 
 
 
• **Lexicography:**
 
 
• Focuses on dictionary-making and the cataloging of words, their meanings, and usage.
 
 
 
• **Semantics:**
 
 
• Deals with the meanings and interpretations of words, phrases, and sentences in context.

question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The reviewer gave a dazzling review of the restaurant, which then went viral.

options.text: A dazzling review of the restaurant was given by the reviewer, which then went viral.
A dazzling review of the restaurant is given by the reviewer, which then went viral.
It went viral when the reviewer gave a dazzling review of the restaurant.
The reviewer was given a dazzling review to the restaurant, which then had gone viral

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of an active sentence becomes the subject of the **passive sentence.**
 
• The verb form changes **to accommodate the new subject.**
 
• The phrase** "was given"** correctly converts the active verb **"gave"** into passive form.
 
• The additional clause** "which then went viral"** remains unchanged as it is descriptive.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**A dazzling review of the restaurant was given by the reviewer, which then went viral."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "A dazzling review of the restaurant is given by the reviewer, which then went viral." – This option is incorrect because the verb "is given" is in the present tense, while the original sentence is in the past tense.
 
• **Option 3:** "It went viral when the reviewer gave a dazzling review of the restaurant." – This option is incorrect because it does not express the sentence in passive voice.
 
• **Option 4:** "The reviewer was given a dazzling review to the restaurant, which then had gone viral." – This option is incorrect because it incorrectly places "the reviewer" as the object and uses an incorrect verb form.

question:

options.text: The agenda had been finalized by them.

The agenda will have been finalized by tomorrow morning.
The agenda will be finalized tomorrow.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Future Perfect tense** in the active voice ("**will have finalized**").
 
• To convert Future Perfect from active to passive, the structure used is: **Object + will have + been + past participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• The object "**the agenda**" becomes the new subject, and "**will have finalized**" changes to "**will have been finalized**."
 
• Option 3 is the only choice that maintains the correct tense and follows the passive voice formula for the future perfect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The **agenda will have been finalized** by tomorrow morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Past Perfect Passive):** "had been finalized" is used when the original sentence is in the past perfect tense.
 
• **Option 2 (Simple Past Passive):** "was finalized" is used for converting sentences originally in the simple past tense.
 
• **Option 4 (Simple Future Passive):** "will be finalized" is the passive form for the simple future ("will finalize").

• In the passive voice, the** structure is typically** "object + auxiliary verb + past participle."
 
• The subject **"you"** becomes the receiver of the action, and the verb **"made"** is in the** past participle (v3)** form.
 
• The preposition** "by" **indicates the doer of the action, which is omitted in this sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

•

• To convert a Future Continuous sentence into the passive voice, the structure is: **Object + will + be + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• In this sentence, the object "**the implications of the findings**" becomes the subject, and the verb "**evaluating**" becomes "**being evaluated**."
 
• Option 1 correctly follows this grammatical structure, making it the accurate passive transformation.

The committee is expected to have resolved the jurisdictional ambiguities before the policy rollout.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The committee is expected to have resolved the jurisdictional ambiguities before the policy rollout."
 
• This sentence uses an introductory phrase ("is expected") followed by a **Perfect Infinitive** ("to have resolved").
 
• To convert the Perfect Infinitive to passive voice: Change "to have + past participle" to **"to have been + past participle."**
 
• Place the object "the jurisdictional ambiguities" at the beginning. Since this subject is plural, the introductory verb changes from "is expected" to **"are expected"** for subject-verb agreement.
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the committee."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The jurisdictional ambiguities are expected to have been resolved by the committee before the policy rollout."*

• **Option 3: **"...should have been resolved..." – Incorrect because it changes the meaning/mood from a statement of expectation to a statement of obligation ("should").
 
• **Option 4: **"...were resolved..." – Incorrect tense (Past Simple) and changes the noun "ambiguities" to "clauses."

solution:

• The given sentence is written in the future continuous tense.

• The future continuous tense in the passive voice has the following structure: __Object+ shall/will + be + V3 + by subject__

• Change the subject into an object.

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject (the doer) performs the action, followed by the verb and the object.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "When **was America discovered by Columbus** and later **it was renamed** after Amerigo Vespucci?"

• **First part:** The passive "was [subject] discovered by [agent]" becomes the active interrogative "did [subject] discover [object]." Thus, "When was America discovered by Columbus" becomes "When **did Columbus discover** America."
 
• **Second part:** The passive "it was renamed" has an implied agent (people/they). In active voice, we use "they renamed it."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

subject: ENG
question:
Choose the correct active voice form from the given options.

The laptop may not be bought by her.

options.text: She may not buy the laptop.
She might not buy the laptop.
She should not have bought the laptop.
She may not have bought the laptop.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject of the sentence performs the action of the verb.
 
• To convert from passive to active: Identify the agent (the person performing the action), which is "her." In the active voice, the pronoun "her" changes to the subject form **"She."**
 
• Identify the modal and tense: The sentence uses the modal **"may"** in a negative passive construction ("may not be bought").
 
• The active form of a modal in the present/future is "Modal + (not) + base verb." Therefore, "may not be bought" becomes **"may not buy."**
 
• The subject of the passive sentence ("The laptop") becomes the object in the active sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She may not buy the laptop."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "She might not buy..." – This changes the modal from "may" to "might." While similar in meaning, the active voice should preserve the specific modal used in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "She should not have bought..." – This changes the modal to "should" and the tense to the **Past Perfect Modal** form, which expresses a missed obligation or regret.
 
• **Option 4:** "She may not have bought..." – This is the **Perfective Modal** form, which suggests a possibility about an action in the past, rather than a present/future possibility.

The advisory panel might have been overlooking critical discrepancies in the data prior to the audit.

Critical discrepancies were being overlooked by the panel prior to the audit.
Critical discrepancies might have overlooked the panel during the audit.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive Voice Transformation:** To convert a sentence with a complex modal tense, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Modal Perfect Continuous Tense** (Active: *might + have + been + verb-ing*).
 
• The structure for **Modal Perfect Continuous Passive** is: **Object + modal + have + been + being + Past Participle + (by + Subject)**.
 
• **Sentence Breakdown:** 
 
 
• **Active Subject:** The advisory panel
 
• **Active Verb:** might have been overlooking
 
• **Active Object:** critical discrepancies in the data
 
 
 
• In the passive version, "Critical discrepancies in the data" moves to the subject position, and "might have been overlooking" becomes "might have been being overlooked."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Critical discrepancies in the data might have been being overlooked by the advisory panel prior to the audit."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Critical discrepancies were being overlooked..." – This uses the **Past Continuous Passive**, losing the "might have" modal aspect of the original statement.
 
• **Option 3:** "Critical discrepancies might have overlooked the panel..." – This is an **active voice** construction that makes the "discrepancies" the ones doing the looking, which is logically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "Critical discrepancies had been overlooked..." – This uses the **Past Perfect Passive** and changes the timeframe from "prior to" to "during."

• Always use the **third form** of the main verb in passive form.

 ​

• Change the passive verb "had been painted" to the active form "had painted."
 
• Place the original subject "the house" after the verb as the object.

• **Passive to Active Voice Conversion:** In this transformation, the object of the passive sentence (which is the recipient of the action) becomes the object of the active sentence, and an agent (like "They") is introduced as the subject.

• The entire noun phrase **"the roads and bridges that connect many important cities in India"** must stay together as the object to avoid "misplaced modifiers" (which happen when a descriptive phrase is too far from the word it describes).

question:
Change the following from active to passive:

The panelists would have reconsidered the proposal had new evidence been submitted.

options.text: The proposal would have been reconsidered by the panelists had new evidence been submitted.
The proposal would reconsider by the panelists had new evidence been submitted.
The proposal could be reconsidered by the panelists had new evidence been submitted.
The proposal was under reconsideration by the panelists had new evidence been submitted.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The panelists would have reconsidered the proposal had new evidence been submitted."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the proposal" at the beginning as the new subject.
 
• Change the active verb form "would have reconsidered" (conditional perfect) to "would have been reconsidered" (conditional perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the panelists."
 
• The conditional clause "had new evidence been submitted" remains unchanged as it is already in an inverted conditional structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The proposal would have been reconsidered by the panelists had new evidence been submitted."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The proposal would reconsider..." – This remains in the active voice and is grammatically incorrect as a proposal cannot perform the action of reconsidering.
 
• **Option 3:** "The proposal could be reconsidered..." – This changes the modal auxiliary from "would have" to "could be," which alters the intended meaning and tense.
 
• **Option 4:** "The proposal was under reconsideration..." – This uses a prepositional phrase to describe a state rather than converting the specific verb structure to the passive voice.

• Transformation of Infinitives: The structure of it is as follows:
 
 
• Subject+is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had+to+V1+Object. 
 
• Subject(Objective case)+is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had+to+be+V3+by+object(subjective case). 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Your child is to learn chess. (Active Voice)*
 
• *Chess is to be learnt by your child. (Passive Voice)*

subject: ENG
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The shop owners were requested to close the shops by the agitators.

options.text: The agitators request the shop owners to close the shops.
The agitators have requested the shop owners to close the shops.
The agitators are requesting the shop owners to close the shops.
The agitators requested the shop owners to close the shops.

solution:
The correct answer is: **The agitators requested the shop owners to close the shops**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **subject **of the Passive Voice is changed into the **object** of the Active Voice. Also, the **object** of the Passive Voice is changed into the **subject** of the Active Voice.
 
• The **removal** of the **helping verb** and the preposition **'by' **is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.
 
• The Passive voice in this question is in **Past Indefinite**. Thus, the Active voice will also be in **Past Indefinite**.
 
• In Passive voice, the format is: **Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)**.
 
• Thus, the format of Active voice is: **Subject + V2 + Object.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)
 
• Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)
 
 
 
• The options except (4) don’t follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***The agitators requested the shop owners to close the shops***.

question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The car hit the pole beside the shop before the accident.

options.text: The pole beside the shop were hit by the car before the accident.
The pole beside the shop was hit by the car before the accident.
The pole beside the shop had been hit by the car before the accident.
The pole beside the shop hit by the car before the accident.

solution:
The correct answer is: **The pole beside the shop was hit by the car before the accident.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In order to convert an** active sentence to a passive sentence**, we need to make the object of the active sentence the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In this case, the object of the active sentence is **"the pole beside the shop".**
 
• The subject of the active voice **'the car' **will become the object of the passive voice.
 
• We also need to use the appropriate form of the verb **"to be" **and the past participle of the main verb **"hit". **
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Therefore, the correct passive sentence is** *"The pole beside the shop was hit by the car before the accident." *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because "were" is not the correct form of the verb "to be" to use with "pole".
 
• **Option 3 **is incorrect because "had been hit" implies that the action happened before another past action, which is not the case in this sentence.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because it is not a grammatically correct passive sentence.

subject: ENG
question:
In the clause:

“...believing itself to have attained certainty,”

What grammatical structure is “believing” a part of?

options.text: A finite verb in past tense

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**believing**" is a **present participle** (the -ing form of a verb used as an adjective).
 
• In the phrase "**believing itself to have attained certainty**," it functions as a **participial phrase** that modifies the noun phrase "each stage of consciousness."
 
• A participial phrase acts as an **adjectival modifier**, providing extra information about the subject without functioning as the main finite verb of the sentence.
 
• It is non-finite, meaning it does not show tense or person on its own and requires a main verb ("encounters") to complete the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Structural Breakdown:** *"...each stage of consciousness [Noun Phrase], **believing itself to have attained certainty [Participial Phrase modifying the noun phrase]**, encounters [Main Verb] its own inadequacy."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: A relative clause** – A relative clause typically begins with a relative pronoun like "which" or "that" (e.g., "which believes itself...").
 
• **Option 2: A passive voice** – Passive voice would require the past participle and a form of the verb 'to be' (e.g., "is believed"). "Believing" is in the active form.
 
• **Option 4: A finite verb in past tense** – A finite verb functions as the main verb of a clause and shows tense. The past tense of believe is "believed." "Believing" is a non-finite form.

• **Sentence 3** comes next, detailing what she noticed after answering the phone: 
• "She heard her friend's voice on the other end."
 
• **Sentence 4** concludes the sequence with the resulting action: 
• "They started talking."
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is **1-2-3-4**.

subject: ENG
question: Which sentence contains a correct use of the **passive voice** from the passage?

options.text: "The Author creates the meaning of the text."
"The text is furnished with a final signified."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive voice structure:** The subject of the sentence receives the action instead of performing it. The formula is: **Subject + form of 'to be' + Past Participle**.
 
• In the sentence *"The text is furnished with a final signified,"* the subject is **"The text."**
 
• The verb phrase **"is furnished"** consists of the auxiliary verb "is" (form of to be) and the past participle "furnished."
 
• The "text" is not performing the action of furnishing; it is the recipient of that action, which is the defining characteristic of the passive voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The text is furnished with a final signified."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The Author creates the meaning of the text." – This is in the **active voice** because the subject (The Author) is performing the action (creates).
 
• **Option 2:** "Language speaks the Author's intentions." – This is in the **active voice** because the subject (Language) is performing the action (speaks).
 
• **Option 3:** "Writing begins when the Author speaks." – This contains two clauses, both in the **active voice** (Writing begins; Author speaks).

question: Identify the correct passive voice sentence from the passage:

options.text: The fire brigades fought the fire bravely.
A large part of the market was destroyed.
The strong wind helped the fire.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The subject of the sentence receives the action instead of performing it. The formula is: **Subject + Form of 'to be' + Past Participle**.
 
• In **Option 2**, the sentence is: *"A large part of the market was destroyed."*
 
• The subject "A large part of the market" is the recipient of the destruction.
 
• The verb "was destroyed" consists of the auxiliary verb "was" (past tense of 'to be') and the past participle "destroyed."
 
• The performer of the action (the fire) is omitted, which is a common characteristic of the passive voice when the cause is known from the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A large part of the market was destroyed."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The fire brigades fought the fire bravely." – This is **active voice**; the subject (fire brigades) performed the action (fought).
 
• **Option 3: **"The strong wind helped the fire." – This is **active voice**; the subject (strong wind) performed the action (helped).
 
• **Option 4: **"Authorities are investigating the cause." – This is **active voice** in the present continuous tense; the subject (authorities) is performing the action (investigating).
